# Apereo CAS documentation (development)

> Apereo CAS is an enterprise identity provider and single sign-on server for the web, with support for CAS, SAML2, OpenID Connect, OAuth2, WS-Federation, multifactor authentication, delegated authentication and more. Each link below points to a Markdown copy of a page of the development documentation; the same address ending in .html is the page itself.

Each feature page lists the settings it uses; the configuration catalog has all of them.

- [Configuration catalog](https://apereo.github.io/cas/assets/data/development/index.json): every CAS and third-party setting with its type, default value, description and module, as JSON
- [Settings changes](https://apereo.github.io/cas/assets/data/development/settings-changes.json): settings added, removed, replaced or given a new default since 8.0.x, as JSON

## Planning

- [Architecture](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/planning/Architecture.md): The building blocks of a CAS deployment: the CAS server, CAS clients, supported protocols and the web, ticketing and authentication subsystems.
- [Getting Started](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/planning/Getting-Started.md): A practical path to planning a CAS deployment: collecting use cases, studying the architecture, building an overlay and asking for help.
- [Quick Start](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/planning/Quick-Start.md): Build CAS in eight guided steps with passwordless and delegated login, SAML2, OIDC, MFA, LDAP, Redis, interrupt and Palantir.
- [Getting Involved](https://apereo.github.io/cas/developer/Contributor-Guidelines.html)
- [Security Guide](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/planning/Security-Guide.md): Security considerations for running CAS: transport security, dependent systems, cookie and ticket encryption, throttling, security headers and session controls.
- [Upgrade Guide](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/planning/Upgrade-Guide.md): How to plan and execute a CAS upgrade: choosing the target version, comparing overlays, reviewing release notes and testing changes.
- [Release Notes](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/release_notes/Overview.md): Release notes for each release candidate of the current CAS development line, with new features, changes and fixes.
- [Release Policy](https://apereo.github.io/cas/developer/Release-Policy.html)
- [Release Schedule](https://github.com/apereo/cas/milestones)
- [Maintenance Policy](https://apereo.github.io/cas/developer/Maintenance-Policy.html)

## Installation

- [WAR Overlays](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/WAR-Overlay-Installation.md): Install CAS with a WAR overlay: generate a project, add modules, override configuration and UI, and build a deployable cas.war.

- [WAR Overlays: Upgrade Recipes](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/OpenRewrite-Upgrade-Recipes.md): OpenRewrite is a tool and platform used by the CAS allows the project to upgrade installations in place from one version to the next. It works by making chan...
- [Command-line Shell](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/Configuring-Commandline-Shell.md): Use the CAS command-line shell to look up settings and modules and run other utility commands against a CAS installation.

- [Graal VM Native Image](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/GraalVM-NativeImage-Installation.md): Build and run CAS as a GraalVM native image for faster startup and a smaller memory footprint, with the limitations that apply.
- [Kubernetes Helm Deployment](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/Kubernetes-Helm-Deployment.md): Deploy CAS on Kubernetes with the Helm chart from the CAS Initializr, using a local cluster as the worked example.
- [Servlet Containers](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/Configuring-Servlet-Container.md): Choose and configure a servlet container for CAS: embedded Apache Tomcat or Jetty, or an external container.
- [Servlet Containers: Options: Embedded](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/Configuring-Servlet-Container-Embedded.md): Note that CAS itself ships with a number of embedded containers that allow the platform to be self-contained as much as possible. - [Servlet Containers: Options: Embedded: Apache Tomcat: Rewrite Valve](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/Servlet-Container-Embedded-Tomcat-RewriteValve.md): The rewrite valve rewrites request URLs using mod_rewrite-style rules before they reach CAS.

- [Servlet Containers: Options: External](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/Configuring-Servlet-Container-External.md): Remember that an external container’s configuration is NEVER automated by CAS in any way which means you are responsible for upgrades, maintenance and all ot...
- [OS Service](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/Configuring-Deployment-System-Service.md): Run CAS as an operating system service with init.d or systemd on Linux, or as a Windows service.
- [Troubleshooting Guide](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/Troubleshooting-Guide.md): Answers to common CAS deployment problems: logging, redirect loops, missing attributes, unauthorized services, expired tickets, memory and TLS errors.

## Administration

- [Overview](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/Admin-Dashboard.md): Palantir, the CAS admin dashboard, for managing registered services, inspecting sessions and tickets and operating the server from the browser.
- [MCP Server](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/Admin-MCP-Server.md): Expose CAS as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so AI assistants and agents can look up applications, tickets and people.

- [Authentication Policy](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Configuring-Authentication-Policy.md): Authentication policies that decide when an authentication transaction succeeds, such as requiring all handlers or a specific handler.
- [Authentication Policy: Global](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Configuring-Authentication-Policy-Global.md): Global authentication policy that is applied when CAS attempts to vend and validate tickets.
- [Authentication Policy: All](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Configuring-Authentication-Policy-All.md): Satisfied if and only if all given credentials are successfully authenticated. Support for multiple credentials is new in CAS and this handler would only be ...
- [Authentication Policy: Any](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Configuring-Authentication-Policy-Any.md): Satisfied if any handler succeeds. Supports a tryAll flag to avoid short circuiting and try every handler even if one prior succeeded.
- [Authentication Policy: Groovy](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Configuring-Authentication-Policy-Groovy.md): Decide whether an authentication attempt succeeds with a Groovy script that inspects the authentication result and can reject it with an exception.
- [Authentication Policy: Not Prevented](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Configuring-Authentication-Policy-NotPrevented.md): Satisfied if and only if the authentication event is not blocked by a PreventedException.
- [Authentication Policy: Required](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Configuring-Authentication-Policy-Required.md): Satisfied if and only if a specified handler successfully authenticates its credential.
- [Authentication Policy: REST](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Configuring-Authentication-Policy-REST.md): Contact a REST endpoint via POST to detect authentication policy. The message body contains the CAS authenticated principal that can be used to examine accou...
- [Authentication Policy: Source Selection](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Configuring-Authentication-Policy-SourceSelection.md): Allows CAS to select authentication handlers based on the credential source. ## Authorization

- [Overview](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authorization/Authorization-Overview.md): The authorization options in CAS: service access strategies, external policy engines and the Heimdall authorization engine.
- [Heimdall](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authorization/Heimdall-Authorization-Overview.md): Heimdall, the CAS authorization engine for APIs: policies, resources, the AuthZEN evaluation API and integration with gateways and proxies.
- [Heimdall: Authorization Requests](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authorization/Heimdall-Authorization-Requests.md): How to send an authorization request to Heimdall, with the request payload, the responses and the AuthZEN evaluation API.
- [Heimdall: AuthZEN](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authorization/Heimdall-Authorization-AuthZEN.md): AuthZEN support in Heimdall: decision context, access evaluations, search and policy decision point metadata.
- [Heimdall: Authorization Principal](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authorization/Heimdall-Authorization-Principal.md): How Heimdall identifies who is asking for access: the tokens and credentials an authorization request may carry.
- [Heimdall: Authorization Resources](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authorization/Heimdall-Authorization-Resources.md): How to register the APIs and resources Heimdall protects, grouped by namespace in JSON files.
- [Heimdall: Authorization Policies](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authorization/Heimdall-Authorization-Policies.md): The policies Heimdall can attach to resources, from required attributes and scopes to Groovy, REST, JDBC and OpenFGA.
- [Heimdall: Gateway Integration](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authorization/Heimdall-Authorization-Gateway.md): Use nginx as a policy enforcement point that asks Heimdall to authorize each request before passing it upstream.
- [OpenFGA](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/services/Service-Access-Strategy-OpenFGA.md): Authorize access to applications registered with CAS by sending a check request to OpenFGA.
- [Cerbos](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/services/Service-Access-Strategy-Cerbos.md): Authorize access to applications registered with CAS by sending a resource check request to Cerbos.
- [SCIM](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/services/Service-Access-Strategy-SCIM.md): Authorize access to applications registered with CAS using group memberships looked up from a SCIM server.
- [Permit.io](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/services/Service-Access-Strategy-PermitIO.md): Authorize access to applications registered with CAS by syncing the user to Permit.io and asking it for a decision.
- [Permify](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/services/Service-Access-Strategy-Permify.md): Authorize access to applications registered with CAS by sending a check request to Permify.
- [Open Policy Agent](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/services/Service-Access-Strategy-OpenPolicyAgent.md): Authorize access to applications registered with CAS by evaluating Open Policy Agent policies.
- [AWS Verified Permissions](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/services/Service-Access-Strategy-AWS-VerifiedPermissions.md): Authorize access to applications registered with CAS by sending an authorization request to Amazon Verified Permissions.

## Multitenancy

- [Overview](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/multitenancy/Multitenancy-Overview.md): Run several isolated tenants on one CAS server, each with its own URL, authentication strategy, policies and settings.
- [Tenant Registration](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/multitenancy/Multitenancy-Tenant-Registration.md): How tenants are registered with CAS: the JSON tenant definition file, and how to supply your own tenant registry.
- [Tenant Capabilities](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/multitenancy/Multitenancy-Tenant-Capabilities.md): The fields of a tenant definition: authentication, attribute resolution, protocol, delegated authentication and user interface policies.
- [Tenant Properties](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/multitenancy/Multitenancy-Tenant-Properties.md): Give a tenant its own CAS settings, such as an email server, authentication handlers or attribute repositories, with the properties map of its definition.
- [Performance](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/multitenancy/Multitenancy-Performance.md): How CAS builds tenant resources at runtime, what that costs under load, and how many active tenants the current design suits.

## Delegation & Proxying

- [Overview](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Delegate-Authentication.md): Delegate authentication from CAS to external identity providers such as SAML2 IdPs, OpenID Connect providers, other CAS servers and social logins.
- [Authentication Policy](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Delegate-Authentication-AuthenticationPolicy.md): Restrict which external identity providers each registered application may use for delegated authentication.
- [Auto Redirection](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Delegate-Authentication-Redirection.md): Redirect users straight to an external identity provider instead of showing the provider selection menu.
- [Discovery Selection](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Delegate-Authentication-DiscoverySelection.md): Let users discover and select an external identity provider, for example by email domain, before delegating authentication.
- [Profile Selection](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Delegate-Authentication-ProfileSelection.md): Let users pick which linked account or persona to use when a delegated login matches several CAS profiles.
- [Provisioning](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Delegate-Authentication-Provisioning.md): Provision and link user profiles returned by external identity providers into identity stores such as SCIM or a REST API.
- [Post Processing](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Delegate-Authentication-PostProcessing.md): Adjust external identity providers before they are shown to the user, such as titles, icons and redirect URLs.
- [Request Customization](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Delegate-Authentication-Request-Customization.md): Customize the authentication requests CAS sends to external identity providers at runtime.
- [Identity Provider Registration](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Delegate-Authentication-Provider-Registration.md): Register external identity providers with CAS for delegated authentication, and the list of supported provider types.
- [Identity Providers: Apple](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Delegate-Authentication-Apple.md): Let users log in to CAS with their Apple ID through Sign in with Apple.
- [Identity Providers: Microsoft Entra](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Delegate-Authentication-Azure-AD.md): Let users log in to CAS with their Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) account through OpenID Connect.
- [Identity Providers: CAS](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Delegate-Authentication-CAS.md): Let users log in through another CAS server, which acts as the external identity provider for this one.

- [Identity Providers: X (Twitter)](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Delegate-Authentication-Twitter.md): Delegate authentication to X, the service formerly known as Twitter. The provider is still named Twitter in CAS settings and client names.
- [Identity Providers: GitHub](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Delegate-Authentication-GitHub.md): Let users log in to CAS with their GitHub account.

- [Logout & SLO](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/Logout-Single-Signout.md): Logout and single logout (SLO) in CAS: ending the SSO session and notifying applications by back-channel or front-channel requests.

- [Account Management: JDBC](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/password_management/Password-Management-JDBC.md): The account password and security questions may be stored inside a database.
- [Account Management: REST](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/password_management/Password-Management-REST.md): Tasks such as locating users’ email and security questions as well as management and updating of the password are delegated to user-defined rest endpoints.

- [Access Strategy: Cerbos](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/services/Service-Access-Strategy-Cerbos.md): Authorize access to applications registered with CAS by sending a resource check request to Cerbos.

## Impersonation

- [Overview](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Surrogate-Authentication.md): Surrogate authentication (impersonation): let an authorized user log in to applications as another user.
- [Account Selection](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Surrogate-Authentication-AccountSelection.md): How an impersonating user chooses the surrogate account, with a login syntax or a selection screen.
- [Access Strategy](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Surrogate-Authentication-AccessStrategy.md): Control which applications allow impersonation and who may impersonate whom.
- [Session Expiration](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Surrogate-Authentication-Session-Expiration.md): Give impersonation sessions their own, shorter expiration policy.
- [Principal Resolution](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Surrogate-Authentication-Principal-Resolution.md): Resolve the surrogate user's principal and attributes during impersonation.
- [Audits](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Surrogate-Authentication-Audit.md): Audit records and email or SMS notifications for impersonation events.
- [Account Storage: Simple](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Surrogate-Authentication-Storage-Simple.md): Surrogate accounts may be defined statically in the CAS configuration.
- [Account Storage: LDAP](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Surrogate-Authentication-Storage-LDAP.md): Surrogate accounts may also be retrieved from an LDAP instance. Such accounts are expected to be found in a configured attribute defined for the primary user...
- [Account Storage: JSON](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Surrogate-Authentication-Storage-JSON.md): Decide who may impersonate whom with a JSON file that maps each user to the accounts they may log in as.
- [Account Storage: REST](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Surrogate-Authentication-Storage-REST.md): Decide who may impersonate whom by calling a REST API that answers whether a user may log in as another account and lists the accounts allowed.
- [Account Storage: Groovy](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Surrogate-Authentication-Storage-Groovy.md): Decide who may impersonate whom with a Groovy script that lists the accounts each user may log in as.
- [Account Storage: JDBC](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Surrogate-Authentication-Storage-JDBC.md): Aside from the usual database settings, this mode requires the specification of two SQL queries; one that determines eligibility and one that is able to retr...
- [Account Storage: Custom](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Surrogate-Authentication-Storage-Custom.md): Decide who may impersonate whom with your own SurrogateAuthenticationService, registered with CAS as a Spring bean.

- [Audits: DynamoDb](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/audits/Audits-DynamoDb.md): Store the CAS audit trail in an Amazon DynamoDB table, so audit records from every node end up in one durable place.
- [Audits: MongoDb](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/audits/Audits-MongoDb.md): Store the CAS audit trail in a MongoDB collection, so audit records from every node end up in one durable place.
- [Audits: Redis](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/audits/Audits-Redis.md): Store the CAS audit trail in Redis, so audit records from every node end up in one shared store.
- [Audits: REST](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/audits/Audits-REST.md): The body of the HTTP request is a JSON representation of the audit record.
- [Audits: AWS Firehose](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/audits/Audits-AWS-Firehose.md): AWS Security Lake is a managed service that centralizes security-related logs and analytics from various AWS and third-party sources. You can send CAS audit ...
- [Audits: Custom](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/audits/Audits-Custom.md): Plug your own audit storage into CAS by registering an AuditTrailManager, and change how client and server IP addresses are recorded with a custom ClientInfo...

## Integration

- [Apache Groovy](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Apache-Groovy-Scripting.md): Use Apache Groovy scripts to customize CAS behavior, and how scripts are loaded, cached and secured.
- [SAML2 Service Providers](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Configuring-SAML-SP-Integrations.md): Built-in SAML2 integrations for common service providers, from cloud apps to SaaS platforms, configured with CAS settings.
- [Google reCAPTCHA](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Configuring-Google-reCAPTCHA.md): Protect the CAS login form from bots with Google reCAPTCHA v2 or v3.
- [Google Analytics](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Configuring-Google-Analytics.md): Send CAS login and user activity to Google Analytics 4.
- [GeoTracking](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/GeoTracking-Authentication-Requests.md): Map authentication requests to physical locations with GeoLocation providers such as MaxMind or Google Maps.
- [GeoTracking: Azure Maps](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/GeoTracking-Authentication-AzureMaps.md): The Azure Maps support is provided by CAS to support location-aware requests. The Azure Maps Java SDK contains APIs that support operations such as searching...
- [GeoTracking: Google Maps](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/GeoTracking-Authentication-GoogleMaps.md): Uses the Google Maps Geocoding API to translate authentication requests into a geo-location.
- [GeoTracking: Maxmind](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/GeoTracking-Authentication-Maxmind.md): Uses Maxmind to translate authentication requests into a geo-location.
- [GeoTracking: Groovy](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/GeoTracking-Authentication-Groovy.md): Use a Groovy script to translate authentication requests into a geo-location.
- [GeoTracking: IP GeoLocation](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/GeoTracking-Authentication-IPGeoLocation.md): Uses the IP GeoLocation API to translate authentication requests into a geo-location.
- [Provisioning: SCIM](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/SCIM-Provisioning.md): The SCIM standard is created to simplify user management and provisioning in the cloud by defining a schema for representing users and groups and a REST API ...
- [Provisioning: Apache Syncope](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Syncope-Provisioning.md): CAS may be allowed to provision the authenticated principal via Apache Syncope to a provisioning/identity/entity engine which would then dynamically synchron...
- [Provisioning: Okta](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Okta-Provisioning.md): CAS may be allowed to provision the authenticated principal to Okta. Successful login attempts would allow CAS to pass back the authenticated user profile to...
- [ACME](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/ACME-Integration.md): Obtain TLS certificates for CAS automatically with the ACME protocol, for example from Let's Encrypt. This feature is deprecated.
- [Amazon Web Services](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/AWS-Integration.md): Use CAS to hand out temporary AWS credentials to authenticated users through Amazon STS.
- [CAS Clients](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/CAS-Clients.md): CAS client libraries for Java, .NET, PHP, Apache httpd, Python and other platforms.
- [Swagger](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Swagger-Integration.md): Generate OpenAPI documentation for the CAS REST APIs and endpoints with Swagger and springdoc.
- [JMX](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/JMX-Integration.md): Expose CAS components and settings as JMX MBeans for monitoring and management.
- [Shibboleth Identity Provider](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/integration/Shibboleth.md): Integrate CAS with the Shibboleth identity provider, using CAS as its authentication source or alongside it.
- [JDBC Drivers](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/JDBC-Drivers.md): JDBC drivers and the Hibernate or EclipseLink providers available to CAS features that use relational databases.

## Optional

- [Throttling Authentication Attempts - Failure](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/authentication/Configuring-Authentication-Throttling-Failure.md): All login throttling components that ship with CAS limit successive failed login attempts that exceed a threshold rate, which is a time in seconds between tw...
- [Home](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/index.md): Apereo CAS is an open-source identity provider and single sign-on platform supporting CAS, SAML2, OAuth2, OpenID Connect, MFA and delegated authentication.
- [Ticket Registry Replication Encryption](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/installation/Ticket-Registry-Replication-Encryption.md): Encryption by default is turned off when you use the above ticket registries. It requires explicit configuration before it can be used.
- [Actuator Endpoint - AuditEvents](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Auditevents.md): Exposes audit events information for the current application. Requires an AuditEventRepository bean.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Beans](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Beans.md): Displays a complete list of all the Spring beans in the CAS application.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Caches](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Caches.md): The caches actuator endpoint lists the application caches CAS uses and can clear them.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Conditions](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Conditions.md): Shows the conditions that were evaluated on configuration and auto-configuration classes and the reasons why they did or did not match.
- [Actuator Endpoint - ConfigProps](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Configprops.md): Displays a collated list of all @ConfigurationProperties.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Env](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Env.md): Exposes properties from Spring’s ConfigurableEnvironment.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Health](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Health.md): The health actuator endpoint reports whether CAS and the systems it depends on are up, for load balancers and monitoring tools.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Heap Dump](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Heapdump.md): Returns a heap dump file. On a HotSpot JVM, an HPROF-format file is returned. On an OpenJ9 JVM, a PHD-format file is returned.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Http Exchanges](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Httpexchanges.md): Displays HTTP exchange information (by default, the last 100 HTTP request-response exchanges). Requires an HttpExchangeRepository bean.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Http Trace](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Httptrace.md): The httptrace actuator endpoint from earlier Spring Boot versions no longer exists. Use the httpexchanges endpoint to see recent HTTP requests and responses.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Info](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Info.md): The info actuator endpoint reports general information about the running CAS server, such as build, Java and operating system details.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Logfile](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Logfile.md): Returns the contents of the logfile, if the name or the path of the log file has been set in the logging settings. Supports the use of the HTTP Range header ...
- [Actuator Endpoint - Loggers](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Loggers.md): Shows and modifies the configuration of loggers in the application.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Mappings](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Mappings.md): Displays a collated list of all @RequestMapping paths.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Metrics](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Metrics.md): Shows “metrics” information for the current application.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Prometheus](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Prometheus.md): Exposes metrics in a format that can be scraped by a Prometheus server.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Quartz](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Quartz.md): Shows information about Quartz Scheduler jobs.
- [Actuator Endpoint - SBOM](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Sbom.md): The sbom endpoint provides information about the software bill of materials (SBOM).
- [Actuator Endpoint - Scheduled Tasks](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Scheduledtasks.md): Displays the scheduled tasks in the CAS application.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Startup](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Startup.md): Shows the startup steps data collected by the ApplicationStartup. Requires the SpringApplication to be configured with a BufferingApplicationStartup.
- [Actuator Endpoint - Thread Dump](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/actuators/Actuator-Endpoint-Threaddump.md): The threaddump actuator endpoint returns a snapshot of the threads in the CAS JVM, which helps diagnose hung or slow requests.
- [Elastic Storage - CAS Metrics](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/Configuring-Metrics-Storage-Elastic.md): By default, metrics are exported to Elastic running on your local machine. You can provide the location of the Elastic server via CAS settings.
- [DynamoDb Monitoring](https://apereo.github.io/cas/development/monitoring/Configuring-Monitoring-DynamoDb.md): Monitor the status and availability of DynamoDb databases. This monitor is made available with the usage of a DynamoDb-based module that would for instance m...
